content.value_statement: Failing tests can push teams toward broad, risky changes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to make the smallest passing implementation.
actual_capabilities: Reviews failing tests and error messages before implementation.
Maps each failing test to the smallest required code change.
Applies green phase techniques such as fake it, obvious implementation, and triangulation.
Runs tests after changes and reports pass results.
Records shortcuts and technical debt for the later refactor phase.
limitations: Does not design full architecture or performance optimizations.
Does not replace a red phase test writing workflow.
Requires clear failing tests or error output to guide changes.
May leave intentionally simple code that needs later refactoring.

use_cases.title: Make One Failing Test Pass
use_cases.description: A developer uses the skill to implement only the behavior required by the next failing unit test.

use_cases.title: Keep Pair Programming Focused
use_cases.description: A team uses the skill to avoid broad rewrites while pairing through a TDD session.

use_cases.title: Prepare Refactor Notes
use_cases.description: A maintainer uses the skill to document shortcuts made during green phase work.

prompt_templates.title: Pass the Next Test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the TDD green phase. Review this failing test output and implement the smallest code change that makes the next test pass.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single failing test.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Minimal Implementation
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect these failing tests and choose fake it, obvious implementation, or triangulation. Make only the required changes and run the tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with several related failures.

prompt_templates.title: Limit Scope During Green Phase
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement the minimum passing behavior for these test failures. Do not refactor or add features beyond what the tests require.
prompt_templates.scenario: Team workflow where scope control matters.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Refactor Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Make the failing tests pass with minimal code. Then summarize shortcuts, debt, test results, and the next refactor targets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow before moving to a refactor phase.

output_examples.input: The user provides a failing validation test for an empty product name.
output_examples.output: The assistant adds only the missing validation branch, runs the focused test, and notes that broader validation cleanup belongs in refactor.

output_examples.input: The user provides several failing service tests for user creation.
output_examples.output: The assistant starts with in-memory behavior, confirms the tests pass, and lists database integration as deferred refactor work.

output_examples.input: The user asks to make a route test return a successful response.
output_examples.output: The assistant adds the smallest route handler, verifies the route test, and records any hard-coded behavior for later cleanup.

best_practices: Provide the exact failing test output before asking for implementation.
Run a focused test first, then run the broader suite after changes.
Record every shortcut so the refactor phase has clear targets.
anti_patterns: Adding unrequested features while trying to make tests pass.
Refactoring structure before the failing behavior is green.
Ignoring unrelated failing tests without documenting the reason.

faq.question: What phase of TDD does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports the green phase, where the goal is to make failing tests pass with minimal code.

faq.question: Can it write new tests?
faq.answer: It is not focused on writing new tests. Use it after failing tests already exist.

faq.question: Does it refactor code after tests pass?
faq.answer: No. It records refactor notes, but the actual refactor should happen in a later phase.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide failing test output, relevant source files, and the expected behavior covered by the tests.

faq.question: Does it make production-ready code?
faq.answer: Not always. It favors the smallest passing implementation and may leave cleanup for refactoring.
